Watterson's theta from iSNV count

Source: R/diversity.R
wattersonISNV.Rd

Estimates Watterson's theta (Watterson 1975): $$\hat{\theta}_W = S / (a_n \cdot L)$$ where \(S\) is the number of segregating sites, \(a_n = \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} 1/i\) is the harmonic number, and \(L\) is the genome length, with \(n\) the number of sampled viral genomes.

Usage

wattersonISNV(nSites, genomeLength, meanDepth)

Arguments

nSites

Integer scalar. Number of segregating (iSNV) sites.

genomeLength

Integer scalar. Genome length in bp.

meanDepth

Numeric scalar. Sample size \(n\): an effective number of sampled genomes, not raw read depth. See Details.

Value

Numeric scalar. Watterson's theta estimate.

Details

As tajimaD sets out, raw read depth should not be passed as \(n\) for deep sequencing data: reads are technical replicates of a much smaller viral population, and a depth-sized \(n\) inflates \(a_n\) and makes \(\theta_W\) correspondingly small. Pass an effective sample size, or a depth capped at one, as calcNeutralityTests does.

References

Watterson GA (1975). On the number of segregating sites in genetical models without recombination. Theor Popul Biol 7:256-276. doi:10.1016/0040-5809(75)90020-9

Examples

## n is an effective sample size, not the raw depth
wattersonISNV(15, genomeLength = 13588, meanDepth = 100)
#> [1] 0.000213219
